fullsize_review.method: Opened and visually inspected each active catalog image individually at its native full-size resolution using the image viewer; not a thumbnail/contact-sheet-only review.

assets.observation: Primary style anchor: a continuous coastal village with an ivory-and-walnut tower, teal roof, lush paths and water; warm upper-left light and soft grounded shadows establish the intended world camera/material family.

Two-storey cutaway house with a cyan wireframe expansion volume over the yard; support/floor/door continuity remains illustrative, so I will not derive room geometry, footprint, collision or cost from it.

Multiple connected green islands, stone paths, teal-roof landmarks and docks form a coherent sea scene; its detail/realism is higher than the interior studies and its routes are illustrative, not runtime geography.

A cutaway creative room centers a worktable and selected chair, but the selection marker is baked into the JPEG and the doorway appears to open toward a lower roof; do not reproduce either as production geometry.
A cottage and cyan proposed-room volume sit beside a resource table and medal; the projected room/floor connection is unclear and cannot be treated as a build blueprint or recipe.
One visitor stands at an open garden gate while the house door stays closed and no host appears; this supports a guest-only snapshot composition, not online presence or shared-session proof.

Miu is an orange tabby playing with a coral ball on the garden path near a pergola and climbing ramp; this active pose is baked in, so the requested resting art must be a distinct scene with the same orange-tabby identity.
A gray kitten sits in an open timber nook beside a woven bed and play arch; its coat/face differs from Miu, so it is a separate companion and not a substitute for the orange W10 pet.
The cutaway workshop contains a gear-and-marble-run workbench and a separate tray, but no readable editor, timeline or version controls; mechanical props are concept art, not tested physics.
A single parcel rests on a covered packing stand with a blank tag; this is a gift-corner vignette only and does not supply a friend list, recipient picker, block/report UI or evidence of presence.

The raised square maze shows a generic ivory robot, teal barriers, a coral flag and a blank panel baked at the bottom; neither board geometry nor robot identity is authoritative for the game engine or Robo.
A coral baby dragon faces a lava gap in an intentional side-view with chunky stone platforms; actor/platforms are fused into one illustration and must not become jump physics or collision data.

An ivory generic robot sits beside a deliberately empty plinth in a stone courtyard; the plinth supports neutral outcome states and does not imply a trophy, reward receipt or a shared robot identity with W05 Maze.

Nova (teal outfit, brown ponytail and goggles) stands in a timber/stone learning room with a front-facing board; preserve Nova identity and keep code/output as readable overlays rather than baked or perspective-skewed text.
Use the r35 correction: daylight cutaway 3/4 room with an empty display cabinet and empty plinths; do not use the frontal candlelit original or bake earned trophies into an empty background.
Practice arena uses the source Robo teal/brass identity, with a separate actor pad and grid-like practice floor; it is a concept scene, not live matchmaking, an Arena rules registry or a leaderboard.

layouts_and_states_reviewed.r34_state_definitions: Read the ten scene definitions and declared states; visually reviewed the phone study captures for W03, W05 Maze, W05 Dragon, W06, W07, W09, W10, W10b, W12 and W12b, plus W03 pending, W09 permission-revoked, W10 unsupported and W12 save-error examples.
layouts_and_states_reviewed.r35_visual_captures: Visually reviewed all six synchronized phone captures (W11/W13/W14 at 390x844 VI and 360x640 EN, including 2x text cases), the W14 true-empty capture, and the three original CODE captures for comparison.
layouts_and_states_reviewed.layout_observation: The r35 report records zero horizontal-overflow cases after sync, but the inspected 2x captures still show pathological narrow title wrapping in some headers; do not copy that header treatment. W14 true-empty is separate from earned/locked/secret taxonomy. Controls remain disabled mocks.
layouts_and_states_reviewed.review_limits: Representative screenshots were reviewed; this is not a claim that all 42 r34 states or all 64 r35 browser configurations were individually opened as screenshots, nor that this task ran a browser/device test.

scene_reference_choices.why: W01 fixes the shared stone/wood/light language; W07 lends worktable-scale prop staging but its faulty threshold is excluded; W06 informs a calm, neutral pending-result vignette without implying a grant. W04 journal contents remain separate UI overlays and are sourced from the world-expansion design, not invented economy.

W01 supplies primary palette/materials; only the corrected W14 cutaway/daylight framing is borrowed for a compact timber-and-stone alcove. No achievement cabinet, rewards, or trophy content is reused; controls and language states remain front-facing UI.

W01 anchors the public village arrival and established landmarks; corrected W08 helps keep the tower/island silhouette in the same family. The welcome is a design fixture, not proof of an account/cloud or forced Tutor/purchase gate.

W01 sets shared material/light; W11 is the visual reference for the actual Robo teal/brass identity, not the ivory generic robots in W05 Maze/W06. Scene props and falling-item silhouettes are mapped to catch_stars_module.dart and stars_game.dart; no score, collision, or reward rules are changed.

W01 provides the shared craft/material anchor and W12 the workshop scale; the gear mechanism is not copied as a physics or answer prop. Bitsy identity is controlled by the runtime source (lavender cat, green eyes, grass bow tie and magnifier), not inferred from the older flat village-kit icon.

W01 sets the shared village materials, while W09 and W12b distinguish guest access from the one-parcel gift vignette. The new scene must add a readable fixture friend/recipient list and safety actions instead of pretending the gift stand is the list.

W01 anchors materials; W12 supplies the existing workshop continuity. The requested editor, test zone and version tray are explicit front-facing study UI, not generated mechanics or claims that a marble run has physics.

W01 fixes the world materials; W03 is the one-room project example; W07 supplies the useful workshop furniture scale. Both known door/ghost geometry defects are expressly avoided: this new concept uses a solid continuous floor, a real threshold, and no cyan ghost, and is not a W02 blueprint.

W10 alone defines Miu's orange-tabby garden identity and pergola setting; W10b is used only as a warning against drifting to the gray shop kitten. The rest pose remains a single static scene with baseline behavior, no AI, sadness or purchase pressure.
